LESSON: DIMENSIONING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.2: Dimensioning
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Dimensioning, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in Grade 8 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is dimensioning applied in drawings?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the term dimensioning as used in drawing,

2. use visual aids to categorise the types of dimensioning in drawing (linear, radial, angular, arc),

3. draw types of lines used in dimensioning,

4. discuss the forms of dimensioning as used in drawing (parallel, chain and combined),

5. use appropriate techniques to dimension given shapes in drawings,

6. develop a portfolio of the various dimensioned drawings.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the term dimensioning as used in drawing,
2. use visual aids to categorise the types of dimensioning in drawing (linear, radial, angular, arc),
3. draw types of lines used in dimensioning,
4. discuss the forms of dimensioning as used in drawing (parallel, chain and combined),
5. use appropriate techniques to dimension given shapes in drawings,
6. develop a portfolio of the various dimensioned drawings.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Dimensioning together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: learner acquires team working skills when discussing how to dimension drawings.

● Learning to learn: learner develops organising skills when dimensioning shapes.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when dimensioning shapes.

• Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when discussing how to draw dimension lines.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: learners work together harmoniously when discussing how to dimension drawings.

Link to other subjects

Mathematics: learner relates dimensioning skills to measurement in Mathematics.
